title: Detergent
description: The agent opens the left hand without holding the right closed, and the bottle falls to the floor.
instruction: Place every detergent in the basket.
initial_prompt:
Complete this single task yourself using the tools: Place every detergent in the basket.
Robot: manip/lift2/R5a, two arms and a movable planar base. Left arm is left in the overlook view. EEF poses are local to each arm's planner base: +X forward, +Y robot-left, +Z up; quaternion order wxyz. Fingers extend along tool +X and open along tool Y. Wrist cameras move/rotate with the hands. Measured local EEF z is not height above the tabletop. There is no supplied depth, object pose or camera calibration. Only RGB and measured robot EEF/gripper/base state are available. Base observed yaw is radians; tool command yaw is degrees. You have one continuous conversation and may choose any continuous EEF target, both arms, base motion and waypoint batching. Use execute_eef sequentially, not parallel calls. Use observations to judge motion and object manipulation. The server determines task success independently. Do not start another episode. Resource limits: unlimited tool calls, physics deadline enforced by the server; no hard token limit; resource reminders start after 2,000,000 cumulative tokens. Resource reminders ask you to reduce unnecessary token use while continuing useful work. Select only useful camera views after the initial observation to control resource use. When finished, state the observed outcome concisely.
You may call execute_wam to delegate a manipulation segment to a learned policy. Choose when to delegate using the current scene. It replans every 10 steps and automatically returns control after the requested segment (at most 300 steps). The WAM prompt is fixed to this task's instruction; always pass instruction=null and never invent a per-call prompt. Inspect its returned RGB/state and take over with EEF waypoints or delegate again. Use your own waypoint planning for approach, coordination and recovery as useful. The learned policy uses the same current three RGB cameras plus robot state, and its own frames from earlier in this episode; it receives no object ground truth or demonstration images.
Manipulation guidance: after visually aligning, close at a stationary pose and allow settling. A nonzero finger gap on the table is contact evidence, not proof of a secure grasp. Test each grasp by lifting only 0.01 m first, using motion_steps=16 or more, then hold 8..16 steps and request the active wrist plus overlook views. Keep orientation and base fixed during this test. Check both finger gap and RGB to confirm the object rises with the gripper before further lifting or transport. If it remains on the table or slips, lower and adjust local contact depth/centering using current images. There is no fixed limit on failed grasp attempts; retry or change approach within the remaining experiment budgets. Avoid large instantaneous target jumps while holding an object; use motion_steps for controlled transport. Total steps per waypoint must remain <=64 and includes the ramp. Use only the active wrist for local corrections, adding overlook when establishing alignment, testing grasp, or verifying placement.
RGB inputs are downsampled: overlook 640x360, wrist 384x288; no crop or object annotation.
The saved ICL demonstration remains available through query_icl throughout this episode. Revisit it when the target region, stage order or arm roles are unclear, and when repeated failures or a change of approach make the reference useful. Use view=text for the original annotation and keyframe index, view=frames with frame_indices for selected images, or view=all for the full reference. Indices are zero-based entries in the keyframe index, not source video frame numbers. Querying does not advance simulation. Ground actions in the current RGB/state.

arguments.reason: Approach the first detergent using the learned manipulation policy.
Finish alignment and grasp of the first blue/red detergent.
Test the left grasp with a slow one-centimetre lift before transport.
The first bottle followed the test lift; continue the coordinated handover toward the basket.
Check whether the receiving hand retained the bottle using a small lift.
The receiving grasp slipped; let the learned policy reassess and recover the detergents from the current scene.
Align the left hand and grasp the next standing detergent.
Test the second detergent grasp with a slow one-centimetre lift.
Continue the verified lift and allow the learned bimanual policy to complete the next handover.
Test the transferred detergent with a one-centimetre right-hand lift before transport.
The receiving grasp passed its lift test; place this detergent into the basket and approach the remaining standing bottle.
Finish the basket release and approach the remaining white/green detergent.
Test the white/green detergent grasp by lifting one centimetre slowly.
The white/green bottle moved with the test lift; continue its coordinated handover.
Verify the receiving grasp with a slow one-centimetre lift.
The receiving lift is stable; carry and release the white/green bottle into the basket.
Back away carefully to reveal the dropped blue/red detergent below the counter edge.
Approach the visible dropped bottle from above with the left hand, keeping clear of the counter.
Adjust the recovery viewing angle to center the floor bottle before descending further.
Move closer to the floor bottle with an open angled grasp.
Use a vertical wrist orientation to extend downward within the arm workspace.
The floor bottle is visible but direct downward IK is stalled; use learned dexterity to attempt its recovery.
Reposition the base so the floor bottle is directly below the left arm, reducing reach distance.
Correct lateral base alignment and extend the left hand downward near the dropped bottle.
Attempt a closer vertical recovery grasp at the arm's lower reach boundary.
Try an alternate wrist roll to avoid the stalled lower-arm configuration while reaching for the dropped bottle.
Shift the base forward to bring the bottle under the downward fingers rather than beyond them.
Center the bottle beneath the recovery hand with another small base correction.
Back clear of the counter collision and place the left wrist in a less folded low approach.
Descend from the extended low approach, monitoring reach and clearance.
Retract from the appliance and try a nearly straight-down reach without the forward extension.
Clear the obstructed wrist view before another learned recovery attempt.
Attempt learned recovery of the clearly visible remaining floor bottle from the adjusted base position.
Switch to a right-arm floor recovery approach after the left-arm reach stalled.
Lower the right hand toward the centered bottle with a downward grasp orientation.
Attempt learned fine recovery from the right-hand approach, since both direct low IK approaches reached their limits.

alignment.method: Recorded nonterminal execution chunks in order, one video frame per returned state.

scope: Complete tool-call sequence and initial task prompt of one test episode in the harness with policy.
